parsed.notes: planner_type: _DStar keeps h/k/b/OPEN across steps. _drive repairs it every step with pl.replan, and _seed_all feeds it the changed cells. The only new _DStar instance is created in _planner_for, when the goal key changes or a cached planner is evicted. That is reinit_on_goal_switch, which the rubric excludes from fallback. The stuck path (add_penalty then _seed_all) is an incremental repair, not a restart. The only discard-and-recompute route is the eviction of the least-recently-used planner, which comes back only as a goal switch. map: _GridMap holds a log-odds grid on the instance (update_scan, _transitions) and is not cleared on goal switch. velocity_selection: the nominal path is _carrot, which follows the D* backpointer path from pl.path, and then _choose_dir. _choose_dir scores 72 heading candidates by alignment, clearance and smoothness with no forward simulation, so it is path_following, not rollout_scored. stuck_handling: _start_recovery and the recovery block in _drive send their own commands (back up, rotate in place). That outranks the planning-level add_penalty step. D* checklist: Stentz 1994 form. insert() and min_state() order the heap on (k, x). process_state() separates RAISE (kold < h) from LOWER (kold >= h) and propagates each. seed() is MODIFY-COST: it re-inserts closed states with k = h. replan() stops when k_min >= h(robot) or OPEN is empty, but it also returns on a wall-clock deadline (perf_counter budget), which can end repair before the stopping rule holds, so ds_stop_rule is partial.
